response: {"text":"Strong advocates of the relativity idea argue that there is no room for a universal medium. One prominent commentator on the modern space‑time theory even suggested that space, treated as a fixed physical entity with constant geometry, should be discarded for reasons similar to those that led to the rejection of the universal medium. In this view, only things that can be directly observed count as real. Conversely, many supporters of earlier electromagnetic research treat the universal medium as the fundamental substance, claiming that all mass, momentum and energy are simply manifestations of it. Without delving into deep philosophical debates about what is truly real, most physicists can agree to employ the universal medium as a provisional model that, although imperfect, helps to explain observed phenomena."}
